info.title: wavespeed/seedvr2
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "wavespeed/seedvr2", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for WavespeedAI image upscaling. One component serves both wavespeed/seedvr2 and wavespeed/ultimate-image-upscaler, which take the same request shape.

enable_base64_output.description: If enabled, the output will be encoded into a BASE64 string instead of a URL.

image.description: The URL of the image to upscale.

output_format.description: The format of the output image.

target_resolution.description: The target resolution of the output image.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the WavespeedAI upscalers: the terminal `GET /api/v3/predictions/{prediction_id}/result` document, forwarded unchanged. All three ids are SUBMIT-AND-POLL - `routerresult/classification.go` records each `POST /proxy/wavespeed/api/v3/wavespeed-ai/...` submit as `ReturnModeSubmitPoll`, all three naming the one shared prediction-result poll route - and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished prediction rather than the task handle the underlying submit answers with.
ONE document describes a VIDEO super-resolution model and two IMAGE upscalers, because Wavespeed answers one. `wavespeed/flashvsr` upscales video and `wavespeed/seedvr2` and `wavespeed/ultimate-image-upscaler` upscale images, but all three are polled on the same status route, that route answers the same envelope, and the finished asset arrives in the same `data.outputs[]` list whichever it is. The three ids publish different `example` values for that reason and only that reason.
THE ASSET IS `data.outputs`, a list of STRINGS - not objects with a URL inside, so there is no deeper field to key completion off. Each element is normally a URL to the generated content: an MP4 for `wavespeed/flashvsr`, an image for the two upscalers. The two IMAGE ids can return the bytes INLINE instead: their request schema declares `enable_base64_output`, Router forwards it verbatim, and a caller who sets it receives base64 in these same elements. That is why the element is an unformatted `string` rather than a `uri` - read it as a URI only after checking it looks like one. `wavespeed/flashvsr` has no such field, so its elements are always URLs.
A completed prediction carrying an empty `outputs` is a success that produced nothing, and through Router that case never reaches the caller as this document: Router answers it as a Comfy Router error instead, so a `200` here always carries at least one output.
The URLs are WavespeedAI's own delivery links and they EXPIRE. Router does not re-host this content onto Comfy storage, so what a caller receives is Wavespeed's short-lived URL rather than a Comfy one - download the asset rather than storing the link.
`data.status` is deliberately NOT narrowed to an enum on this surface. Router forwards the field exactly as Wavespeed spelled it and the poll classifier compares it only after lower-casing and trimming, accepting `completed`, `succeeded`, `success` and `done` as terminal successes - so a legitimate success may arrive spelled `Completed` or `succeeded`, which a four-value lower-case enum would reject. A caller that must branch on it should lower-case first and treat any of those four as success.
`code` and `message` are Wavespeed's own envelope-level status, not the transport one; `data.error` is the provider's free-text failure reason and is an empty string on the successful document this schema describes. `data.timings.inference` is Wavespeed's own measurement in milliseconds, not the Comfy charge.

code.description: WavespeedAI's own envelope status code, mirroring an HTTP status (200 on the document this schema describes). Wavespeed reports some failures here rather than in the transport status.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when Wavespeed created the prediction.

error.description: Wavespeed's free-text failure reason, an empty string when there is none. A prediction that genuinely failed reaches a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this document.

id.description: Wavespeed's identifier for the prediction Router submitted and polled.

model.description: The Wavespeed model id the prediction ran on.

outputs.description: The finished generation. Present and non-empty on the document Router returns; this list IS the result. Each element is a URL to the generated content - an MP4 for `wavespeed/flashvsr`, an image for the two upscalers - or, for the two image ids when the request set `enable_base64_output`, the base64-encoded bytes themselves. The links are Wavespeed's own and expire.

status.description: The prediction's terminal state as Wavespeed spelled it. Not narrowed to an enum here: Router forwards the value unchanged and the poll classifier lower-cases before comparing, so a success can legitimately arrive as `completed`, `succeeded`, `success` or `done`, in any case.

inference.description: Inference time in milliseconds. Wavespeed's number, not the Comfy charge.

urls.description: Wavespeed's own links for the prediction.
